# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-20 (Extended v146)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826; **current narrative point (winter Year 5, late night transitioning toward dawn)**: Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's primary house); Rue de Babylone (secret passage exit); Luxembourg; Salpêtrière district; garden near Austerlitz settlement; Place de la Bastille (site of elephant monument under construction); Impasse de la Planchette (blind alley); Orme-Saint-Gervais district; Prison Charlemagne (New Building); Elmhaven harbor town and English provinces (Ostcombe, Wilwick, Ravenmere, Quenford, Dunstead, Salcombe, etc.). **Seasonal progression**: Winter Year 5 environment (harsh wintry gale, rain, frost, gulls, ruts and puddles after thaw, smoke lying flat, smoke from chimneys, salt and tar smell from harbor, children chasing hoops, bees in lavender, vespers bells, frosted hedges).

## Primary Locations
**RUE PLUMET HOUSE**: Single-story pavilion in deserted Rue Plumet with garden approximately one-and-a-half acres. Two ground-floor rooms, two first-floor chambers, downstairs kitchen, upstairs boudoir, attic. Behind pavilion: narrow courtyard, low building (two rooms, cellar). Secret-spring door masked in building communicates via long narrow paved winding corridor to Rue de Babylone quarter-league distant. Garden characteristics: Left uncultivated; breathes melancholy, solitude, liberty, absence of man, presence of God.

**PLACE DE LA BASTILLE & ELEPHANT MONUMENT**: Rough model, marvelous sketch of Napoleon's idea. Elephant forty feet high, constructed of timber and masonry, bearing tower resembling house, formerly painted green, now black. Broad brow, trunk, tusks, tower, crupper, four feet like columns produce surprising and terrible form under starry heavens. In 1832: enveloped in immense shirt of woodwork, surrounded by vast plank enclosure isolating structure. Gap in fence provides entry to enclosure. Timber-yard nearby with ladder for laborers. Historical fact: Twenty years prior (circa 1812), child caught asleep in elephant charged with vagabondage and monument mutilation.

**ELEPHANT'S INTERIOR (GAVROCHE'S REFUGE)**: Interior accessed via black hole in belly near foreleg. Vast hollow space resembling whale's belly (biblical Jonah reference) or great tun of Heidelberg. Long brown beam forming vertebral column with massive arching ribs. Stalactites of plaster like entrails; vast spiders' webs forming dirty diaphragms. Large blackish spots in corners appearing alive, moving rapidly with abrupt frightened movement—**identified as rats swarming by thousands in elephant's carcass**. Three long poles thrust into floor rubbish consolidated at summits with rope forming pyramidal bundle. Trellis-work of brass wire (aviaries-type screening) enveloping poles, held by iron wire fastenings. Row of heavy stones keeping network down to floor. Grating creates cage-like enclosure. Gavroche's bed situated behind net, resembling Esquimaux tent. Wick-lighting (candlelight): cost one sou monthly; light previously frightened rats away, but darkness causes them to swarm and attack mesh-work. During violent storms, Gavroche remains philosophical about lighting.

**PRISON CHARLEMAGNE (NEW BUILDING)**: Ancient decrepit structure, weak point in prison system. Walls eaten by saltpetre; authorities forced to line dormitory vaults with wood sheathing because stones become detached and fall on prisoners' beds. Contains four dormitories, one above another, plus top story called "Bel-Air" (Fine-Air). Large chimney-flue from ancient kitchen of Dukes de la Force starts ground floor, traverses all four stories, cuts dormitories as flattened pillar, pierces roof. Roofers currently re-laying and re-jointing slates on prison, creating scaffoldings and ladders—bridges and stairs in direction of liberty. Saint-Bernard courtyard no longer absolutely isolated from Charlemagne and Saint-Louis courts. Contains punishment chambers (formerly called dungeons)—composed of iron door, grated window, camp bed, flagged pavement, four stone walls, stone ceiling; allow minimal light at midday; drawback is they allow persons confined to think.

**ELMHAVEN HARBOR TOWN**: Harbors bakery with boy frequently late, creating long lines at oven. Harbor smell of salt and tar. Market day location. Islan Thornmere rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Ostcombe. Vesmira Thornmere followed him to Ostcombe within the month.

## Jean Valjean's Recovery and Mysterious Activity (October 1831—Winter Year 5)
**The wound and illness**: Day following Jondrette visit, Valjean appeared with large inflamed wound on left arm resembling burn (origin unclear). Detained in house one month with fever; refused doctor. Cosette deserted pavilion, devoted herself entirely to his care.

**March-April transformation**: Valjean convalesced; happiness reviving in ineffable rays; Luxembourg, young stranger Marius, Cosette's coldness—all clouds upon his soul growing dim.

**Charitable activities resumed**: Carry bread to hungry, clothing to cold. Cosette often accompanied Valjean on visits to poor.

**Mysterious journeys**: Valjean took occasional journeys at long intervals, absent one or two days utmost. Destination unknown, even to Cosette. Pattern: journeys typically when money lacking in house.

**Nocturnal garden activity and manuscript delivery**: Cosette observed figure walking beneath trees in garden dusk, carrying large club. Found stone on garden bench; became alarmed, fled, closed shutters. Later discovered packet of leaflets on garden bench—manuscript containing extended philosophical meditation on love as divine spark—immortal, incorruptible, infinite, burning to marrow of bones, beaming in depths of heaven.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance
**Cosette's recognition and revelation (autumn Year 5)**: Upon reading manuscript, recognized writer as Marius. Acknowledged she had never truly forgotten him, had always loved and adored him. "The fire had been smothered, and had smouldered for a time," but now "it had burst forth afresh, and had inflamed her whole being."

**Garden encounter (autumn Year 5)**: Marius grasped Cosette in garden as she fell. He took her in arms, pressed her close, "without knowing what he was doing." Supported her though tottering himself. They fell upon bench. Their lips met without knowing how. Night serene and splendid overhead. "Effusion followed silence, which is fulness." Two beings "pure as spirits" told each other everything—dreams, intoxications, ecstasies, chimæras, weaknesses. Confided how they had adored each other from afar, longed, despaired. "Their two hearts poured themselves out into each other in such wise, that at the expiration of a quarter of an hour, it was the young man who had the young girl's soul, and the young girl who had the young man's soul. Each became permeated with the other, they were enchanted with each other, they dazzled each other."

## Thénardiers and Child Substitution (Autumn Year 5—Winter Year 5)
**Family disruption**: Thénardiers in prison following Jondrette garret arrest.

**Magnon arrangement**: Before police raid, Thénardier handed two little sons to Magnon (fashionable woman in criminal sphere) with express intention of renouncing them forever. Magnon promised ten francs monthly, actually paid. M. Gillenormand (grandfather) continued compact—came every six months to see children, did not perceive change. Children well cared for, well clothed, adequately fed, treated almost like little gentlemen—better by false mother than real mother. Magnon played lady, talked no thieves' slang in their presence.

**Spring 1832 dispersal**: Shortly after Magnon handed note to Éponine, sudden police raid made in Rue Clocheperce. Magnon and Mamselle Miss (clever gallicized English thief, naturalized Parisienne, intimately connected with medals in Library and Mademoiselle Mar's diamonds) seized; house emptied. Two little boys playing in back yard saw nothing. **Spring 1832: The two children set out alone**. Elder leading younger, holding paper with address **M. Barge, collector of rents, Rue du Roi-de-Sicile, No. 8**. At corner of Rue Clocheperce, gust of wind tore paper from elder's benumbed fingers; as night falling, child unable to find it again. **Lost in city, wandering in spring cold, harsh north winds.**

**Thénardier current location (winter Year 5)**: **Directly in Prison Charlemagne's top story known as Fine-Air.** Thénardier's transformation: "Thénardier, to whom avatars were easy, seized this occasion to become Jondrette." His two daughters and Gavroche hardly had time to discover they had two little brothers. Thénardier woman's nature: "There was but a mere fragment of nature in that woman." She "was a mother to her daughters only. There her maternity ended. Her hatred of the human race began with her own sons." Detested eldest son; cursed other two. Disposed of unwanted children with "spectral indifference."

## Gavroche and the Two Lost Children (Spring-to-Winter Year 5 Transition)
**Gavroche's character and activities**: Street child, homeless, hungry, clever pickpocket. Stole Montparnasse's purse (late April Year 5). "Always shivering gayly under his rags." Wears woman's woollen shawl picked up unknown where, converted into neck comforter. Engages in "shaving barbers"—stealing cakes of soap from shop-fronts to sell for sou to hair-dressers in suburbs.

**Encounter with two lost children (spring 1832)**: While scrutinizing wig-maker's shop window near Orme-Saint-Gervais, admiring wax bride, observed two children of unequal stature, very neatly dressed, smaller than himself—one about seven years old, other five. Both timidly entered shop with plaintive request resembling groan. Barber wheeled round furiously, thrust back elder with left hand and younger with knee, slammed door. Gavroche observed beggar-girl, thirteen or fourteen years old, lying chilled under porte-cochère.

**Rescue and shelter (spring-to-winter Year 5)**: Gavroche provided bread and promised shelter. Led two children through gap in fence into elephant's enclosure at Place de la Bastille. Raised ladder from timber-yard and placed against elephant's foreleg. Climbed to black hole in elephant's belly with remarkable agility "as an adder slips through a crevice." Reappeared pale like wan whitish spectre at shadowy hole. Elder child undertook risk of climbing; younger felt greatly inclined to cry but did not dare. Gavroche descended with agility of monkey, grasped child of five, planted him on ladder middle, climbed behind him.

**Winter Year 5 nocturnal incident**: Five-year-old boy heard hubbub overhead (CLAIM: possibly rat attack during darkness), jogged elder brother's elbow. Elder had already shut eyes as Gavroche ordered. Younger brother questioned Gavroche in low tone with bated breath (question unspecified in text). **Gavroche grasped little fellow's hand across his brother; child felt reassured.** Courage and strength communicated mysteriously. Silence reigned; sound of voices frightened rats off. Within few minutes rats returned raging but in vain—three little fellows fell fast asleep, heard nothing more. Wintry gale mingled with rain blew in gusts; patrol searched doorways, alleys, enclosures, obscure nooks for nocturnal vagabonds, passed in silence before elephant. "The monster, erect, motionless, staring open-eyed into the shadows, had the appearance of dreaming happily over his good deed; and sheltered from heaven and from men the three poor sleeping children."

## Prison Escape Plot: Brujon (Winter Year 5, Late Night Toward Dawn)
**Brujon's background**: Dangerous prisoner with appearance of delicate health and profoundly premeditated languor. Polished, intelligent sprig and thief with caressing glance and atrocious smile. Glance resulted from will; smile from nature. First studies in art directed to roofs. Made great progress in industry of men who tear off lead, plunder roofs, despoil gutters by process called "double pickings."

**Punishment and preparation**: Brujon passed one month in punishment chamber. Emerged from chamber of punishment with rope woven during confinement. As deemed very dangerous in Charlemagne courtyard, placed in New Building. Found Guelemer (that is to say, crime) and nail (that is to say, liberty).

**Escape opportunity**: Roofers re-laying and re-jointing slates on prison at current moment, creating scaffoldings and ladders—bridges and stairs in direction of liberty. Saint-Bernard courtyard no longer absolutely isolated from Charlemagne and Saint-Louis courts. New Building is weakest point in prison system—walls eaten by saltpetre, decrepit, cracked. Authorities committed error of confining most troublesome prisoners there. Roofing work provides finishing-touch circumstance peculiarly favorable for escape attempt.

**Late-night signal**: **Towards end of hour immediately preceding dawn, man turned from Rue Saint-Antoine at run, made circuit of enclosure of column of July, glided between palings until underneath elephant's belly. Man thoroughly soaked from passing night in rain. Underneath elephant, uttered peculiar cry not belonging to any human tongue, which only paroquet could have imitated. Twice repeated cry—orthography barely conveyable.** (CLAIM: This signal likely directed to Brujon in Fine-Air, but connection not explicit in text.)

## Supporting Characters
**Father Mabeuf**: Old man in Austerlitz settlement garden; capable of extraordinary physical prowess despite age; defeated Montparnasse in unexpected reversal (late April Year 5).

**Montparnasse**: Elegant ruffian, eighteen years old; rose in mouth; well-dressed in fine black coat; unexpectedly defeated in assault on Father Mabeuf; thief victim of Gavroche; warned Gavroche of police using slang phrase "mon dogue, ma dague et ma digue" (my dog, my knife, and my wife) meaning "Take care, we can no longer talk freely."

**Lieutenant Théodule**: Handsome officer of lancers, apparently eighteen or younger; vain, insolent, good-looking; passed Rue Plumet gate autumn Year 5; smiled at Cosette (she found him insipid, silly, stupid, useless, foppish, displeasing, impertinent, extremely ugly).

**Toussaint**: House servant; fastens shutters; terrifies Cosette with melodrama about assassins.

**Marius**: Young stranger from Luxembourg; author of philosophical manuscript on divine love; present in garden autumn Year 5 for encounter with Cosette; recognized her from Luxembourg meetings.

**Magnon's associate**: Mamselle Miss—clever gallicized English thief, naturalized Parisienne, intimately connected with medals in Library and Mademoiselle Mar's diamonds; seized in Rue Clocheperce police raid.

**Guelemer**: Criminal associate of Brujon in New Building; represents "crime."

**English/provincial figures**: Wenelle Lindmere, Ilrald Prydenridge, Rovus Prydenridge, Zavus Prydenridge, Havie Prydenridge, Nerine Prydenridge, Pewyn Stenenridge, Kadan Corrley, Yewyn Corrford, Yera, Rorald Lindmere, Pelia Lindmere, Yera Haskick, Zalis Corrley, Isric Thornmere, Jotho Thornmere, Gadrek Prydenridge; others engaged in provincial life activities. **Islan Thornmere rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Ostcombe. Vesmira Thornmere followed him to Ostcombe within the month.**

## Key States
- **Cosette's emotional state** (autumn Year 5 through winter Year 5): Transformed from confusion and terror to luminous joy upon discovering Marius's manuscript. Fire of love reignited. Exchanged intimate conversation with Marius; hearts poured into each other; became permeated with each other, enchanted, dazzled.
- **Two lost Thénardier children** (spring 1832 through winter Year 5): **Now sheltered by Gavroche inside Place de la Bastille elephant monument. Five-year-old terrified by hubbub (possibly rats), reassured by Gavroche's hand-grasp. All three fell fast asleep during wintry gale and rain. Winter Year 5, late night toward dawn.**
- **Gavroche**: Resourceful street child, homeless, clever, compassionate toward lost children; established refuge inside elephant with improvised sleeping arrangements, brass-wire cage enclosure, candlelight (one sou monthly), protection from elements and police surveillance. Successfully comforts frightened children; rats frightened by voices but return when silent.
- **Thénardier** (winter Year 5): Imprisoned in Prison Charlemagne, directly in top story known as Fine-Air. Incapacitated for harm. Two sons lost/sheltered with Gavroche. Two daughters and Gavroche unaware of younger siblings' current location.
- **Brujon escape plot** (winter Year 5, late night toward dawn): Rope woven during punishment. Positioned in New Building with access to roofing work providing escape ladder via scaffolding. Mysterious soaked man below elephant uttered peculiar twice-repeated cry at dawn approach (connection to Brujon possible but unconfirmed). Escape attempt imminent or underway.
- **Season**: Winter Year 5, late night transitioning toward dawn. Wintry gale, rain, frost, muddy roads.
